citation: Lima, F. 2023. Paracheirodon innesi. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2023: e.T49829801A160186246. Accessed on 05 May 2026.

supplementary_info.identification_information: A neon tetra easily diagnosed from its congeners by its color pattern in life and teeth arrangement (see Weitzman & Fink, 1983, 1987).

documentation.range: Paracheirodon innesi occurs in the western portion of the Amazon basin (Weitzman and Fink 1983, Kullander 1986).
documentation.population: The population is supposed to be stable.
documentation.habitats: Paracheirodon innesi occurs in terra firme streams, with clear or dark waters (Weitzman and Fink 1983, F.C.T. Lima pers. obs.).
documentation.threats: The only obvious apparent threat to the species is the harvest for the aquarium trade, however, the great majority of the specimens available in the trade are captive-bred in southeast Asia (Chapman et al. 1997). It occurs across well-preserved aquatic habitats.
documentation.measures: No conservation actions are reported for the species.
documentation.use_trade: Paracheirodon innesi is one of the most popular fishes in the aquarist hobby, and was considered to be the most popular fish in the US aquarist hobby, together with the guppy, Poecilia reticulata (Chapman and Fitz-Coy 1997). The majority of the Paracheirodon innesi in the aquarium hobby are captive-bred in Asia, with less than 5% of the specimens being wild-caught (Chapman et al. 1998).
documentation.rationale: Paracheirodon innesi is considered to be Least Concern (LC) because it has a broad distribution (although somewhat localised) across the western Amazon basin, across well-preserved aquatic habitats. Harvest for specimens for the aquarium hobby is probably not intense enough to be considered a threat to the species.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: This is a valid species (see Weitzman and Fink 1983).
